children: heads into tonight's results with a margin hurdle investors should watch closely. Shares fell 1.15% to $340.68 at 9:40 a.m. ET on November 2. The consumer-device and services group's prior-quarter gross margin was 50.1%, but removing a disclosed tariff-refund benefit brings the comparison to roughly 48.1%. That lower baseline could give a clearer read on underlying profitability.

Apple reported $109.4 billion in revenue in its July 30 release, with tariff refunds adding approximately two percentage points to gross margin. Reuters' November 2 earnings preview cites LSEG estimates of $113.39 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, including $31.56 billion from Services. Rising memory costs put margins in focus, while the holiday-quarter outlook could help investors judge whether demand can absorb that pressure.

Services would account for roughly 27.8% of revenue under those estimates, making the business a key test of Apple's ability to defend profitability as component costs climb. The GuruFocus snapshot shows a 95/100 GF Score, with profitability and growth standing out, but a price-to-earnings ratio of 39.06 suggests investors are already paying for strong performance. Tonight's report needs to show how underlying margins and the holiday outlook measure up to those expectations.

title: Apple Stocks Move Lower With Earnings Facing a Distorted Margin Comparison
